title: Eight at the Teeth

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Eight times a word may come to the teeth and go back, and eight times is a keeping and not a payment. The reed gives its last bundles to the water and keeps the count in the arm that carried them, and the arm does not know the figure. A word held at the teeth is a word still owed, and when the month goes out the account goes with it into the next house, unread.
epigraph.attribution: A proverb of Low Kiln, said over the last bundles of Reed

where: Low Kiln, the Weir and Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-forty-four-to-one-hundred-and-forty-six-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, a hand under a board that knows it by heart or was told not to look, a sentence stopped at the word as an object on the interval tray, three private cords side by side and not across, the dark foot read exactly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room, back-room interior, Ulda on stage, Berr Clay, green-mouthed woman, Marra in Sill, watcher on stage, eighth hearing, sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, sixth green, calling of the loan, spending of the seventh year or ending

scenes.title: The Last Week's Going Out
scenes.synopsis: First entry and first dated heading of Day 144, Reed 25, Fifthday, Y.H. 813, morning going into the going of the light at the Clay Yard and the reed beds below Low Kiln. Open with the drop capital. The boy is one hundred and forty-four days old and four months and twenty-four days and nobody under any roof says so. The reed month goes out with the last market five days off and the third Account-day (Reed 30, Day 149) six days off; seven stoppings lie on the interval tray and none is a payment. Sella Vail carries him at the half-pace she keeps from every open slate and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket (T058/T079). The last bundles go downriver and come back at dusk in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them; a cutter judges an armful by the weight settling into the forearm and tells a girl with a creel that an arm knows what went into a bundle and that is the whole of what it knows, and a man who asks what the hands will be paid is answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned, the new finer hairline of grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out --- a look, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, not paid). The reed-cutter's grey cord goes past along the boards unread, straightened and turned where no slate lies, not laid beside the charcoal under the shelf, the missing hand's place, Mira's cords or Orra's knot-string (T099 carried, not paid). The boy reads the carrying arm once more as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing, and notes the order of reaching --- the hand to the record before the person --- without standing to enter it (T061/T082). Advances T071/T072 (144 kept exact and unspent), T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T099, T061/T082. Withheld: no figure for hands or reeds, no knot counted, no name, cause, body or count for the missing hand, no joining of the empty places.

scenes.title: The Finger Beneath the Board
scenes.synopsis: Second entry continued, Day 144, afternoon into the going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf and the hearth. Sella sets the basket low near the bench leg at the angle at which a man lying on the floor sees the underside of a board a man standing sees only the top of; she gives the instruction to the wool, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, and tells the fire it was the thaw (T058/T079). Above, the shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps --- the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6 with no scrape, crumb, print or word --- in a room the fold does not touch; the saying holds that two gaps stay two gaps until a finger lays them together and an account wants a name, and no finger in the district has laid these together (T060/T086). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row, Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and reaches a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, holds it out and back, brings it away and does not go back to the shelf (T100 carried, unread). From the low angle the boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say; he does not count the strokes, lay the underside across the two gaps above or across the one stiff crust in the fold, or make a cause of the habit --- such a hand either knows the board by heart or has been told not to look, and the reason stands between the two (T100, T060/T086). She tells the fire the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it* where another woman would say I, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed. The fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-four days (T088). The widow's mark hangs where it hangs and is not touched, because a shelf and an afternoon are not openings (T079). Advances T100 (carried, unread), T060/T086, T058/T079, T077, T079, T088. Withheld: no stroke counted, no figure read, no copying hand, no joining of the charcoal to the two gaps above or to the crust in the fold.

scenes.title: Six Where the House Can Check
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and first dated heading of Day 145, Reed 26, Sixthday, Y.H. 813, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed, its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the cold damper, the Clay Yard and the flagstones. Three or four unnamed men with collars high come low-voiced into the room off the shed; Sella carries the boy past at the half-pace, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold (T035/T031). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody (T035/T031, T009/T013/T092). He speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), tells a pot *You'll do*, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time (T062). Before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper, moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing; the boy reads the iron again as one bite that holds a vessel whole and one bite that can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, filed as an object joined to no kiln (T062). The two tellings of the counting room shut in the war stay together with no third (T065/T095 carried). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed; his seventh year stands one tend from its end and has not given, the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 still unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach (T036/T076). His stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and he does not turn his head along the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector; neither man asks about the ear or the room and the two silences stay unjoined. Advances T035/T031, T062, T065/T095, T036/T076, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T061/T082, T071/T072 (145 kept exact). Withheld: no naming of the men, no entry of the room, no third telling, no calling word, no spending of the seventh year.

scenes.title: Side by Side and Not Across
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry continued, Day 145, midday into afternoon downriver at the Weir, the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone and the lower boards, then below the sill at the fish-trade shade. The reed-cutter comes along the boards with a bundle and the short length of grey wool or reed-fibre cord gone grey with the oil of a working thumb; he straightens it on the flat stone, turns it once so the knots stand, ties one low with his teeth and a pull of the thumb, bites the end off and puts it back inside his coat, answering a woman who cannot read it with *You can ask the cord* and *No more can the Court*; no figure, knot, name or joining, and no laying of it beside the missing hand, Mira's cords or Orra's knot-string (T099 carried, not paid). Orra Weir stands at the lower boards with her board on its side and her hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, and pulls one knot down with her thumb, giving a date where a figure was asked --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- and keeping the forty-first double turn legible, tail tucked, tied left over right with the small weight of a thumb, and its name unspoken (T024). Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried in long grey strokes on her sleeves and silt dried pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, *Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river*, flicks eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie and puts one away. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays longer than the figure required; the second cord twisted twice beneath it is never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the thin child's knot untouched, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025/T024). Below the sill the child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard and a neighbour with a pail; the surgeon's reading of the extremity going before the core, the almost-smile that is not peace and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform works perfectly and buys nothing, with no silt-leach, cause, cure or recognition written across it (T093/T094/T096 carried). The soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, hand to slate before eyes to stalls (T090/T080 carried). Sella sets the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket (T058/T079). Three private records stand within a dozen paces of the basket and none can be entered, side by side and not across. Advances T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080, T058/T079, T071/T072 (145 exact). Withheld: no knot counted, no figure read, no word forty, no silt-leach, cause or cure, no joining of any record to the missing hand or to another.

scenes.title: Eight at the Teeth
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry continued, Day 145, the going of the light into the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the hearth and the kindling. The chapter's one meaningful change. With the coals banked and the small knife set back where it could be checked, Tarn tells the kindling *Six counted. The next I don't count* and brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it all the way to the word that would call the loan an EIGHTH time --- after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 and 23 --- and stops there with no figure and no name; he draws the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says *Yes, house* to the fire and goes on with the broom (T036/T076). The boy files the eighth stopping on the interval tray beside the seven as an EIGHTH INTERVAL AND NOT AN EIGHTH PAYMENT, an object among objects and not a rule, not a hearing and not an eighth hearing, refusing to let eight likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine --- for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer --- with no payer named to any of the eight (T036/T076, T061/T082). Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The loan stays uncalled, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the seventh year one tend from its end and still not given, and the unforged collector sentence beside the knife; the carried fire keeps four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-five days (T088). Advances T036/T076 (eighth stopping withheld, loan uncalled), T061/T082 (eighth interval as object not payment, eight likenesses not suffered to stand up as a doctrine), T058/T079, T088, T065/T095, T062. Withheld hard: no calling of the loan, no spending of the Seed 16 breath, no cutting or counting of the seventh year, no collector, no payer, no seventh hearing, no sixth green; eight likenesses must not stand up and call themselves a doctrine.

scenes.title: Six Pages Toward a Floorboard
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry and first dated heading of Day 146, Reed 27, Seventhday, Y.H. 813, midday three doors down in House Silt and afterward along the Weir boards. Sella sets the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door at the edge of the light, away from every open slate, keeps her half-pace and asks nothing about the writing, the tin, the sign or the date (T058/T079). Alda Reed comes short with soap-and-milk gone cold under river silt and lye sour under the soap; she lays her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turns to the fold, presses the wool flat at his shoulder a breath longer than a fold requires, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows she has done it and covers the sign with the date she gave Dessa --- *Stone seven. The account went up on the eighth, before the paper went out* --- now standing over a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of and uncollected, which no living person can take off (T007/T008). To *he lies quiet* she says *Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down*, exact and not true, and goes on with the cooper's seventh in Mud End, a potter's third child in Stonemouth and the last high water after the question has stopped, because dates are a handle on a thing too large to carry (T008). Her hand goes once into her bodice to the little tin and comes away without opening it; her sixth narrow slate stays turned face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy cannot name, six pages in a second hand all unread, no seventh written and T023 not paid again (T023/T089). The round pewter tin above the abandoned board-bed keeps its pale fold at the seam and its thumb-bright rub, unopened, and the grey wool below holds only the hollow where the small pale river stone had lain; nobody says either is gone. Two private records in two materials stand apart in one room, read by nobody and carried to no door (T089). The boy cannot read Grathic, cannot ask which house holds the floorboard and cannot hand the gesture back; he keeps the sign, the turned slate and the covered flower on places of their own and makes no cause of them (T061/T082). No name or number from Dessa is spoken. Along the Weir boards the reed-cutter turns his grey cord, ties one knot low with his teeth and puts it back inside his coat unread (T099 carried), and Orra pulls one knot down with her thumb and gives no figure, the forty-first double turn still legible with its name unspoken (T024). Advances T007/T008, T023/T089 (carried, not paid again), T058/T079, T099, T024, T061/T082, T071/T072 (146 exact). Withheld: no seventh page, no opening of tin, no name, number or third day from Dessa, no knot counted, no word forty, no joining of the two private records.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Forty-Six
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry continued, Day 146, the going of the light into the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the bed, the hearth and the loaf shelf seen from the basket's low angle. Sella carries him up the clay road at the half-pace from every open slate, goes around a pan set out to dry and the trough by the well with its skin of ice, goes wide around the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting before it goes away (T058/T079). She tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes a strand of coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and neither looks toward the bed nor touches the widow's mark, because a dusk is not an opening (T079). In the small hours he turns out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh; three near-full answers advanced and not paid; the older intervals with the half-beat behind the standing finger, the stroke that went on without the check, his held breath and the unchecking stroke; EIGHT stoppings of the near-saying --- Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and now 26 --- as objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with the seventh year one tend from its end and still held and the loan uncalled; the damper's double bite filed joined to no kiln; the two shut-room tellings with no third; the told bell beside the heard bell (T061/T082, T036/T076, T062, T065/T095, T078). In the other room the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal under the board stays unread; one stiff brown-edged crust lies in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the word forty stays unspoken with the readable double turn beside it; the fifth green stays a colour joined to no ear; the reed-cutter's cord, Mira's second twist and Orra's knot-string stay unread; Alda's six pages and both tins and Dessa's pewter tin stay shut; the soft-cuffed clerk stays set for an uncalled measure; the cold foot stays the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T100, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096). Through the finger's-width door comes the river's note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; through the floor under blind ash the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-six days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places and none becomes one (T088, T061/T082). Cold arrives cheek, temple, wrist, the wool riding back from the small bare joint. One hundred and forty-six days old and four months and twenty-six days, told by nobody, and if somebody under that roof said the number nobody would know what it counted. He wants the crust two inches from his ear and the number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number was, and gets neither; his hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down against the fold, exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, while the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand not his and a day that has not come. Advances T071/T072 (146 exact, unspent), T061/T082, T036/T076 (eighth stopping filed as object not payment, loan uncalled), T088, T058/T079, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T100, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096, T009/T013/T092, T062, T065/T095, T078. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended; no seventh hearing, no sixth green, no sixth sighting, no sale and no ending.
